extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners/staff involved in appeals and judicial review
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements governing judicial review (appeals and civil actions) from Patent Trial and Appeal Board decisions, including filing, service, timing, extension, and USPTO/internal office procedures following court action. Covers appeals to the Federal Circuit and civil actions under 35 U.S.C. 145 and 146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with the final decision in an appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under section 134(a) may appeal the Board’s decision to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit; by filing such an appeal the applicant waives his or her right to proceed under section 145.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applicants appealing PTAB final decisions; waiver of 35 U.S.C. 145 when appealing under 141 is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of Reexaminations and Post-Grant Proceedings to the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner dissatisfied with the final decision in an appeal of a reexamination or a party to an inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, or derivation proceeding who is dissatisfied with the final written decision may appeal the Board’s decision only to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (with limited exceptions for derivation proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exclusive appellate route for these proceedings; derivation proceedings have special election provisions to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 146 in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil action to obtain patent (35 U.S.C. 145)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a PTAB decision may, unless an appeal has been taken under 141, commence a civil action against the Director in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within the time prescribed by the Director (not less than 60 days). All expenses of the proceedings shall be paid by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil action under 145 permits introduction of new evidence; commencing a 145 action precludes appeal under 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of USPTO regulations governing judicial review (37 CFR 90.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions govern judicial review for PTAB decisions under chapter 13 of title 35 U.S.C.; judicial review of certain inter partes reexamination and interference matters continue to be governed by prior regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to distinctions between types of proceedings and which regulations apply (pre-AIA provisions may continue to govern some reexaminations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal filing and service requirements (37 CFR 90.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal required by 35 U.S.C. 142 must be filed with the Director of the USPTO as provided in 37 CFR 104.2; a copy must also be filed with the PTAB in the appropriate manner (37 CFR 41.10(a),(b) or 42.6(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appealing parties must also comply with Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure and Federal Circuit rules (serving required copies on the court and paying fees). Additional specific service rules apply for appeals from ex parte reexamination, IPR/PGR/CBM/derivation proceedings (must include information to permit the Director to determine whether to intervene and serve per 42.6(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of election to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 146 (37 CFR 90.2(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an adverse party elects to have further review conducted under 35 U.S.C. 146 instead of under 35 U.S.C. 141, that party must file a notice of election with the USPTO as provided in 37 CFR 104.2 and file copies with the PTAB and serve where necessary pursuant to 37 CFR 42.6(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election procedure relevant primarily to derivation proceedings where an adverse party can require civil action under 146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of complaint in a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 146 (37 CFR 90.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The party initiating an action under 35 U.S.C. 146 must file a copy of the complaint no later than five business days after filing the complaint in district court with the PTAB and the Office of the Solicitor pursuant to 37 CFR 104.2; failure may result in further action within the USPTO consistent with the final Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of complaint copies with USPTO is mandatory and failure has consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing notice of appeal or commencing civil action (63 days) (37 CFR 90.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal filed pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 142 must be filed with the Director no later than sixty-three (63) days after the date of the final Board decision; a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146 must be commenced no later than sixty-three (63) days after the date of the final Board decision (subject to statutory exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-appeal timing controlled by Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure; specific rules for elections under 141(d) govern derivation proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time computation, rehearing, and holiday rules (37 CFR 90.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A timely request for rehearing resets the time for appeal or civil action to no later than sixty-three days after action on the rehearing request; if the last day falls on a Federal holiday in D.C., the time is extended pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 21(b). Multiple rehearing requests generally do not reset the time unless ordered by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should note that only timely rehearing requests change the appeal clock and that holidays affect calendar-day deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time standard to seek judicial review (37 CFR 90.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may extend the time for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action if requested before expiration for good cause, or after expiration upon a showing of excusable neglect; requests must be filed per 37 CFR 104.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions follow a standard similar to Federal courts; other USPTO extension/fee rules (e.g., 1.136, 1.550) cannot be used to extend the judicial review filing period after the last decision entry. Requests may be served to the Office of the Solicitor to expedite handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide sufficient information in notices of appeal from IPR/PGR/CBM/derivation (37 CFR 90.2(a)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal arising out of an IPR, PGR, CBM, or derivation proceeding must provide sufficient information to allow the Director to determine whether to exercise the right to intervene in the appeal pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 143 and must be served as provided in 37 CFR 42.6(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must include enough detail in the notice to trigger the Director’s intervention decision; improper or incomplete notices may impede the Director’s ability to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how a notice of appeal is to be filed (Manner of filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Appeal should not be mailed to the Director, the Board, or the examiner; it must be filed in the USPTO by mail to the address in 37 CFR 104.2(a) (actually received by due date), by Priority Mail Express® under 37 CFR 1.10 (date-accepted), or by hand per 37 CFR 104.2(b). A copy and docket fee should be filed with the Clerk of the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable filing methods and cautions against improper delivery; Priority Mail Express allows date-accepted filing treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director and Office of the Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of papers filed in court proceedings in which the Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor either by hand (between 8:30 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. EST to specified address) or by mail to Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO (P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service address may be supplemented to include the attorney's name but must not refer to the Director or USPTO; noncourt papers mailed to this address will be returned without exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative file confidentiality and status during judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative file of an application under judicial review will not be opened to the public by the USPTO unless otherwise available under 37 CFR 1.11; during judicial review the application is not under the jurisdiction of the examiner or the Board unless remanded by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access rules differ from ordinary prosecution; amendments during judicial review are admissible only under 37 CFR 1.198 (see MPEP § 1214.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure following Federal Circuit decision (mandate entry and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Federal Circuit issues its decision, the Clerk forwards the certified mandate to the USPTO which is entered in the file; the mandate date marks the conclusion of the appeal (termination of proceedings as used in 35 U.S.C. 120). The USPTO may not open the administrative record to the public unless otherwise permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Solicitor may request remand to reopen prosecution prior to a CAFC decision; the mandate governs further USPTO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect when all claims are rejected after court mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: If all claims in the case stand rejected, proceedings are considered terminated on the mandate issue date; the case is ordinarily not open to subsequent amendment and prosecution. An applicant wishing to continue prosecution must file a continuation prior to the court mandate entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No revivability by USPTO petition for abandonment caused by outside proceedings; failure to file continuation prior to mandate prevents co-pendency with parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect when some claims are allowed after court mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims are allowed (including those reversed by the Board/court), proceedings are considered terminated only as to claims still rejected; claims indicated as allowable but objected to due to dependency from rejected claims will be treated as rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should either convert dependent claims to independent form via examiner’s amendment and issue the application or set a 2-month shortened statutory period for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form (extensions available under 37 CFR 1.136(a)). If no timely reply, application is abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions and reasons for allowance in office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing on allowed claims, the examiner should set forth reasons for allowance, referring to and incorporating a copy of the appellate brief and the court decision (see MPEP § 1302.14). If formal matters remain, the examiner should take prompt action (examiner’s amendment or Office action with a two-month shortened period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions following court decisions must carefully document the basis for allowance and handle formalities quickly since the application is otherwise closed to further prosecution except for such matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand when court raises unconsidered merits issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the court’s decision brings up for action merits claims not previously considered on the merits (e.g., reversing rejection of generic claims where nonelected species were present), the examiner will take the case up for appropriate action on such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remand may require further examination of issues the PTAB/court addressed; remand procedures and potential reopening of prosecution follow MPEP § 1214.07 and Office of Deputy Commissioner approval where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening of prosecution after court decision (approval and procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Office action proposing to reopen prosecution after a court decision must be forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for written approval, which will be indicated on the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening prosecution is controlled and requires internal USPTO approval; see related MPEP sections for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of appeal consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: After an appeal is docketed in the Federal Circuit, failure to prosecute (e.g., failure to file a brief) may result in dismissal by the court; appeals may also be dismissed on motion of appellant and/or Director. Court proceedings are considered terminated as of the mandate date; after dismissal, USPTO action follows the same procedures as after a CAFC decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status of the application or reexamination after dismissal depends on circumstances leading to dismissal; examiners should follow the 'Office Procedure Following Decision' guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil suits under 35 U.S.C. 145 and 146 — initiation and service (MPEP § 1216.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: A civil action under 145 or 146 is commenced by filing a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within the time specified; copies of the complaint and summons must be served timely on the Director, the U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, and the Attorney General per Rule 4(i) FRCP. The party initiating a 146 action must also file a copy of the complaint with the Board within five days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All expenses of 145 actions are paid by the applicant; subpoenas for application/reexamination files should be hand-carried to the Office of the Solicitor; termination dates and appeal periods are governed by 37 CFR 1.197(b) and may be ascertained from the Office of the Solicitor when material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence introduction in 35 U.S.C. 145 actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action under 145, the plaintiff may introduce evidence not previously presented to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differentiates 145 civil actions from appeals under 141 (review on the administrative record) and affects litigation strategy and USPTO handling of returned files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena procedures for district court requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Any subpoena by the district court for an application or reexamination file should be hand-carried to the Office of the Solicitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure prompt, proper handling and delivery of subpoenaed materials to the Office of the Solicitor to comply with court orders and USPTO internal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director’s right to intervene and remand requests by the Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has the right to intervene in appeals from derivation proceedings and IPR/PGR/CBM under chapter 31/32 per 35 U.S.C. 143; the Solicitor may request remand to the USPTO and reopening of prosecution prior to the CAFC decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of appeal must include sufficient information for the Director to decide on intervention; the Solicitor’s remand requests may affect whether prosecution is reopened before mandate entry.
